sentences.text: Agilisaurus is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived in eastern Asia during the Middle Jurassic Period. The only known species is Agilisaurus louderbacki, found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan, China.
This animal grew to be approximately 1.2 to 1.7 meters long, 60 centimeters tall at the hip, and weighed around 40 kilograms.
It possessed leaf-shaped teeth adapted for an abrasive, plant-based diet, featuring wavy tooth enamel previously thought to be unique to hadrosaurs, suggesting it was more resistant to wear.
The only known specimen, the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in 1984 during the construction of the Zigong Dinosaur Museum.
The genus and species were named by Peng Guangzhou in 1990 and described in detail in 1992.

With a tibia measuring 20.7 cm and a femur measuring 19.9 cm, Agilisaurus was likely an extremely fast bipedal runner that used its tail for balance, though it may have walked on all fours while feeding.
Some paleontologists suggest Agilisaurus may have been a burrow dweller because it lacked tail-stiffening bony struts.
Agilisaurus was originally classified in the family Fabrosauridae, a group no longer considered valid by most paleontologists.
One recent analysis places Agilisaurus basal to heterodontosaurs on the branch leading to Marginocephalia.
The parent group of the genus is Neornithischia, and the genus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
